Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Pakistan’s board has unveiled its new central contracts after a long delay. PCB snubs Test skipper from T20I contract A number of familiar faces have disappeared from Pakistan’s central contracts list for 2026-27, and the biggest surprises are former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood. Opener Imam-ul-Haq has also been left out of the list that the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) released on Saturday. The announcement arrived much later than usual, since the previous set of contracts had run out on June 30. The wait ended with a revamped system, and the changes are bigger than most expected. Test skipper Babar Azam has no T20I contract this time. The batsman has often been under the scanner for his low strike rates in T20s and the recent contract list is another hammer blow to his T20I future. ODI captain Shaheen Shah Afridi sits in the ODI/T20 category, while Sahibzada Farhan, who led Pakistan in their most recent T20 Internationals, has a deal in the T20 group alone. No player has been offered a contract that covers all three formats. The board did not reveal how much each category will pay. It did hand contracts to 38 players, and most of them have landed in a newly created development category. item.title: Seville’s Passionate ‘Gran Derbi’ Divides A City Looking To The Future
item.description: Pablo Fornals of Real Betis celebrates a goal against Sevilla at the Pizjuán last November. Europa Press via Getty Images The last time Real Betis visited Sevilla’s Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán for ‘ El Gran Derbi ’, the game was stopped for more than 15 minutes. Betis won 2-0 that afternoon in November 2025, with second-half goals from Pablo Fornals and Sergi Altimira. Sevilla striker Isaac Romero was sent off and objects thrown from the stands forced the referee to halt play. On Saturday evening, at 6:30pm local time, the Seville derby goes back to Nervión. It is the 13th round of LaLiga, but in Seville nobody treats it as one game among 38. “Here in Seville, football is a way of life, like a religion,” Álvaro Valles told me in a LALIGA press event this week. The Betis goalkeeper was born just outside the city and came through the club’s academy. A rivalry older than LaLiga Sevilla were founded in 1890 while Betis came later, out of a split at Sevilla, and in 1914 a merger created Real Betis Balompié. The first Seville derby was played on October 8, 1915, and Sevilla won it 4-3, and the two side have now met 145 times in official competition. Sevilla lead the record with 66 wins, but have failed to win any of the last three. After November’s heated affair, the return game at La Cartuja in March finished 2-2, after Betis led 2-0 at half time and Alexis Sánchez and Isaac Romero brought Sevilla level. “More than three points” What sets the derby apart is that both clubs carry national weight from the same city. “These are two powerful clubs at national level, and the rivalry is huge,” Valles told international media. “Having two nationally important clubs in the city of Seville makes this match very important all over the world.” Alvaro Valles of Real Betis gestures during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Betis Balompie at BVB Stadion Dortmund. Getty Images Valles has a useful comparison, as Betis are in the Champions League this season, and he has already played at Borussia Dortmund, with a trip to Bayern Munich to come in January. Asked how those atmospheres compare with a Seville derby, he said they are not alike. “A derby is a one-off game. I always say it doesn’t matter what form either team is in. It’s like a final,” he says. “They’re still worth three points like any other game, but against your eternal rival they’re more than three points. It’s the pride of a whole city.” He has lived the rivalry since childhood as Valles grew up in La Rinconada, left the Betis academy to make his name at UD Las Palmas, and came back to the club in 2025 after spending a year in the stands to see out his contract and ensure a move back to his boyhood club. He calls the return “a dream I had wanted to fulfil since I was a kid: playing at home, in my city, for the club of my life.” Two homes in flux The stadiums that built this rivalry are both about to change. item.title: Manchester United rival Liverpool for Italy international defender as club also informed of former midfielder's potential 2027 return
item.description: Atalanta BC v Parma Calcio - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United are rivalling Liverpool for Italy international centre-back Giorgio Scalvini as they plan for life after Lisandro Martinez. The Old Trafford hierarchy have also been alerted to a possible 2027 reunion with former midfielder Scott McTominay amid contract talks at Napoli. Recruitment chiefs scout defensive targets According to TEAMtalk , United are carrying out detailed scouting work on Scalvini as they prepare to reinforce up front, at left-back and in central defence. The Italian has caught the eye of several recruitment departments and could become a major defensive target in 2027, either in January or next summer. That search comes as Martinez enters the final months of his deal, despite a one-year club option. Agent chief questions Barcelona interest Speculation surrounding Martinez's future has gathered pace following earlier claims from the outlet that Barcelona admire the Argentine defender, alongside reports in Spain suggesting he is open to listening to an offer from the Liga giants. However, the president of the Spanish Association of Football Agents, Pedro Bravo, has poured cold water on any potential switch to Catalonia. Addressing the transfer rumours, Bravo said: "Lisandro, as far as I'm aware, neither Deco nor [Hansi] Flick are keen on him." He added that the message coming from Flick and sporting director Deco regarding Martinez is clear: "He's a good player, but we don't like him. He doesn't fit in with us." Regardless of Barcelona's stance, Martinez's contract situation still points towards an Old Trafford exit in the near future. Scottish playmaker considers English comeback Alongside their defensive planning, the report states that former United midfielder McTominay is seriously weighing up a return to the Premier League in 2027. His previous employers have already been notified of the opportunity to bring the academy graduate back to Manchester, and club officials have not dismissed the prospect. The publication's sources believe Napoli remain hopeful of keeping the Scotland international in Serie A, with his current agreement set to expire in 18 months. Because the two parties are currently far apart in contract negotiations, intermediaries have begun pushing him towards potential landing spots in case no middle ground can be found. Injury recovery dictates winter timing Timing will play a decisive role in how United approach both pursuits over the coming months. Because Scalvini has only recently returned from injury, a January move may arrive too soon, meaning United and Liverpool will keep tracking his form before deciding when to bid. Meanwhile, McTominay's ongoing standoff in Italy will determine whether a 2027 reunion becomes a concrete option.

item.title: Cleworth set for 200th Wrexham game
item.description: Defender Max Cleworth has scored 11 league goals in total for Wrexham [Getty Images] Max Cleworth is set to reach another milestone in his Wrexham career this weekend – and the defender is still only 24. A product of Wrexham's academy, Cleworth will make his 200th appearance in all competitions for the club if he features against Lincoln City in the Championship on Saturday (15:00 GMT). "I found out a bit recently that it was coming up," Cleworth said. "It's something I won't think about until maybe after the game and just try and focus on putting in another good performance and another good team performance hopefully. "it's a very proud moment to come through the academy and end up getting 200 games. It's something that, as I said, I'm proud of." Cleworth has played a key role in each of Wrexham's three successive promotions - rising from the National League to the Championship. He made his league debut in manager Phil Parkinson's first game at the helm in August 2021, at Solihull Moors. "That's a game that I look back on with really good memories," Cleworth said. "Obviously, it was the first pre-season of the gaffer's [Parkinson] and then I played a few games in pre-season. "That week's training, I was in and out of the back three. The day before, I was in the set-up team. "That was it really, I told my dad not to bother coming in. I went and played, it was 2-2 in the end." Parkinson cautious on Wrexham trio injury return Injuries, noise & scalps - Wrexham's season so far A shock departure and key results - inside Wrexham's seismic week Cleworth's progress is often used as a marker of the huge strides Wrexham have made under Parkinson and the Hollywood ownership of the club. But Cleworth's first-team debut came before Parkinson's arrival and a whole year prior to Rob Mac and Ryan Reynolds announcing they wanted to buy the club. "I think naturally my debut is one that I'll never be able to forget – Ayr United at home," said Cleworth, recalling the Scottish Challenge Cup tie in September 2019. "Colchester was my first goal in the league. I think it was Gloucester at home in the FA Trophy was my first actual goal, so that one will always stick out. "It's nice to look back on, but hopefully we can make some more memories as we move forward." Having given him his league debut only days after he had turned 19, Parkinson has seen Cleworth develop into one of the club's key players. "It's an amazing story," said Parkinson. item.title: Stephen A. Smith says there’s one rule stopping him from running for President
item.description: Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Sports analyst Stephen A. Smith gives an update on whether he will try to become the next US President. Over the years, Stephen A. Smith has built an impressive fan following thanks to his unfiltered takes on the NBA and NFL. So much so that Smith has now expanded his coverage to things outside of sports, including politics in the United States of America. There have been times when the ESPN analyst has contemplated running for president, but Smith has seemingly given up on that dream. Stephen A. Smith explains why he will not run for US President During a recent podcast appearance with NBA legend Kevin Garnett, Smith talked about a plethora of things. Soon, the conversation shifted to if the ESPN on-air talent wants to run for president. Well, Smith has shut the door on any possibility and it’s because of one important rule. “Listen, would I give all of this up to be the President of the United States of America? Yes, I would. Would I give it up to campaign for the president? H___ no. And according to the rules, you have to give up everything. What they say is you’ve got to give up your money because, by virtue of what I do, let me tell you this: there’s something with the FCC called ‘the equal-time rule,” Smith said. He added, “And equal time means that because of what I do and because I’m on the air all the time, the minute I announce that I’m running, I have to come off the air and give up my career and the money that comes with it. “Now, that ain’t happening, dog. That’s not happening.” Running for president doesn’t automatically mean that Smith will win the election, and if he fails, he could lose relevance among fans. item.title: New Man Utd boss Pochettino sure years in USA made him ‘better coach’
item.description: FILE PHOTO - USA coach Mauricio Pochettino reacts from the touchline during the International Friendly soccer match between USA and Germany at Soldier Field. An overnight flight from Cincinnati to Manchester took Pochettino from his post-match duties after the United States’ win over Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning to United’s Carrington complex, where he has quickly got to work ahead of Sunday’s clash with old rivals Liverpool. Pochettino has been linked with United’s top job before but, while he takes over with the club in the bottom three having won only one Premier League match all season, the 54-year-old believes he is better placed for the Old Trafford challenge now than ever before. “Of course we were missing [club football], we were missing it a lot,” he said. “I think we are animals of the grass. We like to feel the grass, we need to smell the grass and try to help the players to improve every day. “It’s true that it’s a different job when you are in the national team, but at the same time you learn a lot, and I think we are much better coaches now, much better coaches.” Pochettino has plenty of Premier League experience with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, taking Tottenham to both a Champions League and League Cup final, albeit without winning either, and was also a league winner with Paris St Germain. But the man who took the United States to the last 16 of this summer’s World Cup argued the pressure at international level is just as great as in club football. “The expectation and the pressure was massive,” he said. “I remember always in SoFi (Los Angeles), our first game against Paraguay, the pressure was massive, there were more than 200 celebrity people expecting us to win and to play well and all the country was behind us. “They say when you are in the Premier League or in LaLiga or in France, OK, you feel the pressure when you manage this type of size of club. “But being there was, I promise, it was massive pressure, but we found a way to translate that pressure into energy. item.title: Cummins' integrity not compromised - CA
item.description: Pat Cummins was named Australia captain in 2021 [Getty Images] Cricket Australia has "unequivocally rejected" the suggestion that captain Pat Cummins' integrity has been compromised by the sandpaper scandal. On Saturday CA gave its "unanimous support" to Cummins, and he said he would take part in the independent forum set up for players and staff. Cummins has faced claims to step down as captain after Cameron Bancroft's detailed testimony supported claims made by Usman Khawaja that the entire Australia team knew of the plan to tamper with the ball during a Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018. CA and Cummins met this week, with the former saying it was "determined to steward Australian cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn". "We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa," CA said. "We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat's integrity has been compromised." CA chief executive Todd Greenberg said Cummins has been an "exemplary leader" in his five years as captain. "He has consistently spoken and articulated what happened back in 2018 in his version of events. Nothing's changed. Thus, nothing's changing with our captaincy," Greenberg told BBC Sport. Greenberg acknowledged that people's version of events "directly contradict" each other but said Cummins has "not moved one inch" from his story, giving the same account now as he did when interviewed the day after the Cape Town Test in 2018. Cummins is due to lead Australia in the opening match of a four-Test series against New Zealand starting on 9 December in Perth. The pace bowler reiterated his stance that he had no involvement in or knowledge of the sandpaper plot during a 68-minute news conference last week. Cummins has said he will attend the forum that has been set up by CA for players and staff to share their version of events. "I support the forum 100%. I will be there," he said. "All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say. "There will be a lot of difficult conversations, but that is what's needed. "Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority." item.title: An Australian captain who can play for Wales in 2027
item.description: Liam Wright had to wait four years between his fifth and six caps for Australia [Getty Images] Ospreys flanker and once-Australian captain Liam Wright will be at the Principality Stadium today to watch the Wallabies take on Wales in Cardiff. Wright knows that in less than a year, it is possible he could be playing for Australia or Wales at the World Cup in the land of his birth. The 29-year-old has made six appearances for the Wallabies, but his previous game was in July 2024. So despite being capped by the Wallabies, World Rugby regulations would allow him to play for another country three years after his previous international appearance. His eligibility to switch allegiances would start next summer, and just a few months before the World Cup begins in Australia in September 2027. Wright has Welsh heritage, with his grandfather hailing from Pembroke Dock. After more than a year out of professional rugby, Wright moved 12,000 miles to join Ospreys and wants to return to the international stage. "Test rugby is what I want to get to; it's the pinnacle and where I want to play and end up again," he said. Will an international return be for Australia or Wales? Liam Wright played in the back row for Australia against Wales in July 2024 [Getty Images] Which country Wright might play for remains to be seen. When asked about potentially representing Wales, he replied: "I imagine myself playing Test rugby and wanting to do it in a gold jersey, but I'm not going to turn down opportunities anywhere. "If the door is closed for the Wallabies and I'm playing good enough and Wales do come knocking, I'd definitely explore it. "I want to get back playing Test footy [rugby] and play for the Wallabies, but fate has a weird way of working where we've landed in Wales. "I've now got to explore the heritage. I was going past Pembroke Dock the other week and stayed there in an Airbnb and explored the area a bit, which is where my grandfather's from. "Things have a funny way of working out, so I won't rule anything out." Wright will be mindful that Wales and Australia have impressive back-row resources at their disposal. Wales head coach Steve Tandy told the Scrum V podcast in October he had not talked to Wright, who met up with the Australian camp in Cardiff this week. Australia head coach Les Kiss knows Wright well from their Queensland days. "We will always keep an eye on someone of his calibre," said Kiss. "The big thing for Liam was getting back into the game, and I've worked closely with him at the Reds for a number of years. "He was in that gym, in the physio room, throwing everything to get that shoulder right. "I loved the look in his eyes this week. He looked happy again, getting out there, plying his trade and loving the sense of living in a different environment. "I was happy to catch up with him and see how he feels good about himself again." item.title: Monza want €40m for Gustavo Varela, but is he worth it?
item.description: Monza want €40m for Gustavo Varela, but is he worth it? Serie A has several underdog stories blossoming this season on both team and player levels and is all the more worthwhile for it. One such story is of Gustavo Varela, who despite being in his debut season in Italy already looks like a man on a mission. Having scored just seven goals last season in 33 appearances while on loan at Gil Vicente from Benfica, the 21-year-old already has 11 goals in 11 outings this term. These are numbers few were expecting, that too for a team not expected to have a great campaign. Monza are again looking down the barrel, and between their early-season slump and several of their counterparts looking keen to at least put up a fight, things are not looking good for the Brianzoli. But Varela is unquestionably a shining light. Even if he doesn’t manage to help keep Monza up, he is turning enough heads to be able to earn himself a move and not have to try his luck in Serie B. Some even believe a mid-season switch to not be out of question. It would make sense if Monza were to capitalise on his hype knowing they might go down anyway, and there’s previous for this. But is it too soon for Varela? Is he really already worth €40 million. Despite market valuations, the price of a player comes down to however much the buying party is willing to conjure up. And while there are several success stories featuring players who move early and thrive, there are several others — often more frequent — of players who move too early and for too lofty a price tag which they never manage to justify. In recent years alone there are several cautionary tales. Krzysztof Piątek, case in point, looked like the next great striker of his generation before moving to Milan after just half a season with Genoa, and while his numbers mostly remain respectable, the now Al-Duhail man never reached the heights that were expected of him during his short stint at the Marassi. Similarly, Juan Manuel Iturbe, a darling of the video game folk, arrived at Roma amid much fanfare before his career plateaued. After struggling in Europe, he has gone on to have a respectable career in the Americas and is currently at his boyhood club, Cerro Porteño. In fact, one could even argue that Juventus that did not quite get what they were hoping for when they splurged €70 million on Dušan Vlahović to pry him away from Fiorentina in January 2022. All that said, the fact of the matter remains that the current market is a fidgeting, impatient one. Euro ambitions drive return hopes According to talkSPORT , Palace have identified Toney as a winter option after promising Frank the resources needed to strengthen a squad rooted to the foot of the table . Having previously worked under the Danish coach at Brentford, the forward is keen to boost his chances of making England's Euro 2028 squad. Those international hopes recently took a knock when he failed to move a court date clashing with the tournament . Prolific spell highlights goalscoring pedigree Toney left Brentford for Saudi Arabia in a £40 million transfer during the summer of 2024 , departing west London with a proven top-flight record of 36 goals in 85 Premier League appearances. item.title: Harden passes Bryant for 50-point games
item.description: Harden joined the Cavaliers in February after three years with the Los Angeles Clippers [Getty Images] James Harden scored 51 points to move third on the all-time list for 50-point NBA games as the Cleveland Cavaliers beat the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in the NBA Cup. The 37-year-old made all 14 of his free throws as his recorded his 26th 50-point game to move above the legendary Kobe Bryant. Harden, who also made six rebounds and provided six assists at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, had not passed 50 points since scoring 55 for the Los Angeles Clippers in November 2025. Legendary centre Wilt Chamberlain holds the NBA record ⁠with 118 50-point games, while Michael Jordan is second with 31. "When you talk about just basketball, obviously Wilt was elite, but you got Mike and Kobe - shooting guard position, the best to ever do it - so just to be in that conversation, it's very humbling and it's definitely special," said an emotional Harden. Aged 37 years and 86 days, he is the fourth oldest player to score 50 points in a game. "What excites me a lot is even being in my 18th year learning how to still be impactful," said Harden, the ninth highest scorer in NBA history with 29,633 points. "It's easy when you're young - 23, 24, you run around, you jump high and can move fast and get by. Now it's like, you're not as fast. "That's the evolution of James Harden and figuring that out. "Tonight was a confidence-booster that I can do it at a high level still." The Cavaliers travel to the Chicago Bulls in the NBA on Tuesday.

item.title: Tri-West punches ticket to state title game with thrilling win over Indian Creek
item.description: TRAFALGAR - Twelve years since their last state title appearance, the Tri-West Bruins (12-2) broke their dry spell with a 24-21 win over the previously-unbeaten Indian Creek Braves (12-1) in Class 3A semistate action on Friday. The Bruins redeemed a Week 5 loss to the Braves and cried tears of joy after their victory - one win away from being crowned 3A champions. “We worked so hard since we were little kids and we spoke it into existence that if we didn’t win or at least didn’t go to state this year, it was a failure,” said Tri-West senior Carter Cummings. “We really took that to heart and I think it shows man.” Tri-West needed under two minutes to draw first blood. After a good return put them at their own 45, senior quarterback Jack Sorgi took the snap 11 yards for a touchdown. That closed out a seven-play drive with 8:11 left in the opening frame. “That first drive was very important because all week we stressed how good their defense was,” said Tri-West coach Jason Ward. “This is a top defense and just showed Indian Creek that we can move the ball on them. Just kind of make them second guess themselves (like),’ Can we stop them tonight?’ It’s hell of a team. One good defense, and yes, that first drive was very important.” The Braves fumbled on a punt return, which gave the ball back to the Bruins. item.title: Harry Kane out for a ‘few months’ as Bayern Munich confirm ankle ligament tear
item.description: Harry Kane faces the "next few months" on the sidelines after suffering a torn left ankle ligament during Bayern Munich ’s 1-1 draw against Cologne on Friday. The injury occurred when Cologne defender Joel Schmied intercepted Michael Olise’s low cross at the back post, clattering into the Ballon d’Or winner’s left leg on the follow-through. Though the England captain got back to his feet after treatment, he was unable to continue and hobbled off the pitch accompanied by two physios. Following an assessment by the club’s medical team, Bayern confirmed Kane had sustained a torn syndesmotic ligament and "will therefore be sidelined for the next few months". It is a major setback for Kane, who won the Ballon d’Or last month and then became the most-capped England men’s player of all time last week, surpassing the previous record held by Peter Shilton. Kane received treatment but was unable to continue on Friday night (Getty) Kane scored 73 goals last season to earn the Ballon d’Or and had made a flying start to the current campaign, registering 10 goals and 10 assists in 16 games for Bayern across all competitions. He also scored eight goals in six Nations League games to help England top their group as he took his overall international tally to 93 goals in 127 caps. England learned on Friday that they will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, which will be a rematch of the two teams meeting at the same stage of the World Cup back in July. Thomas Tuchel’s side won that game 2-1 thanks to a brace from Jude Bellingham, and the two-legged quarter-final will be played in late March. Kane will hope that he is back in time for that tie, but Bayern’s statement indicates that he will not be seen on the pitch for the remainder of 2026 or the early weeks of 2027. Kane’s injury is a real blow for Bayern (Tom Weller/PA) Bayern also suffered another injury blow on Friday night as Michael Olise failed to return for the second half. The club issued an update on Olise’s condition after the game. The statement read: “Michael Olise has been diagnosed with a contusion of the foot. The French attacking player will receive treatment over the coming days.”

item.title: B1G volleyball tournament brings Illinois freshman back to hometown roots
item.description: FISHERS — The entirety of Friday has been a surreal experience for Hamilton Southeastern High School grad Madi Miles. Now an outside hitter for the Illinois volleyball team, the 6-1 freshman is back in her hometown for the inaugural Big Ten volleyball tournament, which began this weekend at the Fishers Event Center. The Illini made the two-hour bus ride from Champaign on Friday morning, allowing Miles to take in all the familiar sights as they headed to the venue. That in itself was a "weird" and "crazy" experience, Miles said. And then they arrived at the facility. The 2025 Indiana Miss Volleyball finalist estimates she ran into at least five people she knew while walking around the events center, the encounters ranging from former teachers and the dad of former high school teammate Jasmine Daniels, to Fishers mayor Scott Fadness and former HSE athletic director Jim Self, who grabbed a photo with Miles before the team departed for practice. "It's been really cool seeing all the familiar faces — and that's just today," Miles said. "We don't even play (tonight), so I can't wait to see what Saturday's going to be like." As the regular season began winding down, Miles' high school coach, Jason Young, was pushing for Hamilton Southeastern to host Illini practices for the duration of their stay. "My mom was in contact with him and keeping me updated," she laughed. "It's so weird being back," Miles later added. The entire team strolled the athletic corridor, checking out pictures of their teammate from her days as a two-time Class 4A state champion with the powerhouse Royals. Inside the gym, the video boards displayed a graphic welcoming Miles home with her two most recent team photos and the message "Once a Royal, always a Royal." And, yes, the team made sure to get a photo with the signage before starting practice. "My teammates are amazing," Miles said. "They've been really helping me and pushing me." Those teammates, she continued, have helped fuel her recent run of success, maintaining trust in her and feeding her balls in spots where they know she can be successful. To wit, Miles racked up 106 kills over an eight-match stretch between October and November, then collected six kills, two digs and two blocks in the regular-season finale at Iowa. For the season, Miles has 129 kills (.204 hit%), 29 digs and 10 blocks in 44 sets played for the seventh-seeded Illini, who open against Washington at 6 p.m. Saturday. "Everyone on this team trusts each other and everyone likes to push each other and make each other better," she said. "That really helps." However, the Ducati rider has another chance over the Portuguese Grand Prix weekend, which he himself has described as his “first real championship match point”. With 74 points still available (37 in Portimao and 37 in Valencia), the Spaniard holds a 60-point advantage over Jorge Martin and a 74-point lead over Marco Bezzecchi, meaning he could mathematically clinch the world championship on Saturday after the sprint race. The scenarios for Marc Marquez to clinch the 2026 title at the Portuguese GP are straightforward, as they depend solely on his own results. In general, Marquez cannot lose more than 23 points to Martin over the weekend, meaning he would clinch the title if he outscored the Spaniard by two points across the weekend. item.description: Chelsea threaten Barcelona’s plans to sign long-term centre-back target – report Barcelona’s pursuit of Alessandro Bastoni has become more complicated after Chelsea have emerged as serious contenders for the Inter Milan defender, creating additional competition for one of Hansi Flick’s preferred defensive targets. According to recent reports from TEAMtalk , Chelsea have entered the picture as they assess options to strengthen their defence, while Barcelona continue to remain interested in the 27-year-old Italian international. Bastoni’s situation in Italy could become increasingly important over the coming months. Notably, his current agreement with Inter expires in 2028, and the Italian club would prefer to secure an extension rather than risk entering the final year of his contract without an agreement. However, with several European heavyweights monitoring his situation, Inter face an important decision over his future next summer. Chelsea’s interest complicates Barcelona’s pursuit Chelsea have entered the race for Alessandro Bastoni. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) Chelsea’s involvement is a significant development for Barcelona, particularly because the Premier League club can offer considerable financial resources. Now under former manager Xabi Alonso, the London side is looking for a left-footed centre-back, just like Barcelona. In fact, Bastoni’s representatives have already assessed Chelsea as a potential destination, with discussions taking place as part of their evaluation of the market. The report also suggests that Barcelona’s interest has become a bit doubtful because of uncertainty over whether Flick fully supports the proposed signing . That uncertainty could prove important, as Bastoni wants assurances about his role before committing to a move, meaning Barcelona would need to explain to him that he has a central place in their sporting project. Inter want to secure Bastoni’s future Inter Milan want to renew Bastoni’s contract. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Amid all this, Inter are aware that Bastoni’s contractual position could attract further attention if negotiations over an extension remain unresolved. His existing deal expires at the end of the 2027/28 season, meaning he would be able to negotiate a pre-contract agreement with foreign clubs from January 2028 if he did not renew. However, Inter are not necessarily preparing to sell, knowing that Bastoni himself has previously been described as comfortable in Milan. The possibility of a departure is therefore dependent on the outcome of future negotiations over a new contract and not the number of interested clubs.

item.title: United States expected to host 2028 Copa America in second consecutive edition on American soil
item.description: Argentina v Colombia - CONMEBOL Copa America USA 2024: Final - Getty Images Sport Organisers are formalising plans for the United States to stage the 2028 Copa America, with an official announcement anticipated soon. The tournament will mark the second straight edition of South America's premier international competition held on American soil. Confederations finalise joint hosting talks According to The Athletic , all parties now expect the 2028 competition to return to the US following extensive discussions between CONMEBOL and CONCACAF that began in December 2025. Anonymous sources confirmed the host nation is not yet finalised, while Brazilian publication Globo also reported on Friday night that an announcement is imminent. Once confirmed, the US will have hosted three of the last five editions between 2016 and 2028. Commercial success outweighs previous controversies When the two confederations jointly organised the 2024 tournament, all 10 South American nations were joined by six CONCACAF guests: the US, Mexico, Canada, Panama, Costa Rica and Jamaica. Over 1.5 million supporters attended the 16-team event, which generated the majority of CONMEBOL's $319 million in national team competition revenue that year. However, the 2024 edition also drew scrutiny. Players and coaches criticised stadium playing surfaces, while Argentina's 1-0 final win over Colombia at Miami's Hard Rock Stadium was delayed by roughly 80 minutes due to dangerous crowd issues. The hosts also exited at the group stage, leading Gregg Berhalter to be replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, who coached the team at the World Cup before joining Manchester United . Packed calendar shapes summer scheduling The report states that CONCACAF nations will again have a pathway to qualify in 2028, though the exact number of spots and qualification process remain unspecified. Scheduling will require careful coordination because Los Angeles hosts the Summer Olympics starting on July 14, 2028, the exact calendar date of the 2024 final, with the US football team set to compete under coach Steve Cherundolo. Fortunately, domestic league clashes should be avoided, as Major League Soccer switches to a European-style calendar from 2027-28, ending campaigns in late May. The tournament extends a remarkable run of major events in the US, following the 2025 Club World Cup, the 2026 World Cup, and a joint bid with Mexico, Jamaica and Costa Rica for the 2031 Women's World Cup. Formal confirmation awaits confederation decision Formal confirmation of the 2028 hosts is expected shortly, though a CONMEBOL press officer noted no official statement had yet been received and CONCACAF declined to comment. Meanwhile, the CONMEBOL council met on Friday to reiterate its backing for FIFA president Gianni Infantino ahead of upcoming elections. Next week will also see the joint 2031 Women's World Cup hosting bid officially confirmed.

item.title: Macau GP: Rashid Al Dhaheri defeats Mattia Colnaghi to take qualification race win
item.description: Motorsport photo Rashid Al Dhaheri took victory in the Macau Grand Prix qualification race after jumping polesitter Alex Ninovic at the start and resisting a final-lap attack from Mattia Colnaghi. Rodin racer Ninovic had set the pace during a heavily disrupted opening qualifying session on Thursday that featured five red flags, before Friday's Q2 was rain-affected, but the Australian did not make a great launch from pole and was instantly under pressure from Al Dhaheri. The R-ace GP driver - who finished fourth in the Formula Regional European Championship standings this year - had grabbed the lead before the first turn, while Red Bull Junior Colnaghi demoted Ninovic to third on the run to Lisboa. Colnaghi, who looked rapid in first practice but could not replicate that during the chaotic qualifying, then set about closing the gap to Al Dhaheri. This was 1.1 seconds by the end of the first tour and continued to fluctuate between just below and just over a second for much of the contest. But Colnaghi suddenly closed to within half a second on the penultimate tour and mounted an attack into Lisboa for the final time but was never able to draw alongside his rival. MP Motorsport competitor Colnaghi therefore had to settle for a front-row start for Sunday's main race, finishing just 0.251s behind across the line. Mattia Colnaghi Mattia Colnaghi Ninovic drifted away from the lead duo to end up 3s back from Al Dhaheri but last year's GB3 champion was never under pressure for third, while Pinnacle Motorsport driver Enzo Deligny was fourth. Williams junior Kean Nakamura-Berta was fifth for much of the race but was passed by Indy NXT frontrunner Tymek Kucharczyk in the closing stages. For all the drama during qualifying, the race was relatively incident-free with the only significant clash coming on the third lap when Taito Kato tagged Kabir Anurag out of Lisboa, which damaged the suspension on the latter's RPM machine. Although this forced Anurag to stop on track, his car was quickly cleared without need for a caution. Also in strife was Sebastian Wheldon, who pulled into the pits at mid-distance having struggled at the wheel of a new chassis after his original car split in two pieces following a crash in the Esses that caused one of the multiple qualifying stoppages.
